question: Which Linux companion app direction should OpenClaw pursue now that Windows Hub is shipped, and what should happen to the competing open Linux app candidates?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: choosing C/GTK, Rust/GTK, another route, or deferring Linux companion work affects ownership, security review, packaging, release validation, and long-term app support.

options.title: Choose one Linux app track
options.body: Pick the preferred Linux implementation direction, require security/package proof, and review or adopt one PR while closing or redirecting the other track.

options.title: Defer the Linux companion app
options.body: Keep Linux Gateway support documented, close broad app PRs for now, and split only narrowly scoped Linux platform gaps into separate issues.

options.title: Keep multiple tracks experimental
options.body: Allow the competing Linux app PRs to remain exploratory while making clear that no in-repo companion app will land until a maintainer-owned architecture decision is made.

recommendation.title: Choose one Linux app track
recommendation.body: Pick the preferred Linux implementation direction, require security/package proof, and review or adopt one PR while closing or redirecting the other track.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue and current platform status wording both route through steipete's product-direction comments and recent platform docs commit.
